To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we have collected a large scale dataset of hand kinematics from 8 subjects performing 20 daily life tasks in a studio flat setting, (ii) we have applied our Sparse Motion Analysis approach on the data to derive spatio-temporably localised modes of motion that are invariant to amplitude and time scales, and (iii) we have mechanically implemented the most common SEMs on a dexterous robotic arm and demonstrated stable grasps of daily life objects in open-loop control.
1. The Sparse Motion Decomposition (SMD) approach can be used to extract a set of sparse, time-scale invariant control primitives from natural, unconstraining daily life kinematics data.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the brain controls the human hand using sparse control primitives.

the development of a new approach to understand the dexterous control of the human hand, which is based on the extraction and implementation of sparse control primitives from natural hand motion data.
the question of how we can emulate the dexterity of the hand, and how can we use the human hand as an inspiration for the design of dextrous robotic hands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown for the first time that SEMs extracted directly from human hand kinematics, and implemented on a robotic hand, result in stable grasps.
our SEMs are an effective control strategy for robotic grasps.
the SEMs extracted from the daily life kinematics of the human hand can be used to generate a stable grasp of different objects in an open-loop control of the dexterous robotic hands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SEMs are a sparse symbolic code for the brain to encode continuous hand motions.
the SEMs extracted from natural human behaviour are a promising control primitives to emulate complex dexterous hand manipulation.
SEMs can be used to design novel control strategies for dexterous robotic hands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SEMs extracted from natural human hand behaviour can be implemented as a sparse control strategy on a dextrou robotic hand.
the SEMs extracted from natural hand kinematics can be implemented on a dexterous robotic arm and can be used for stable grasp of objects in open-loop control.
the SEMs extracted from human hand motions are a promising approach for the development of dexterous robotic hands.
